featured_reviews.name: Priyanshu Deshraju
featured_reviews.review_text:
Updated: This review is subjective, because I had joined the classes (1 month verbal crash course) around 11th November, about 1.5 months before my actual GMAT. and I had also taken only one test offered in the class. (out of 5-6)  Additionally, I had not attended the Quant classes , but had access to few online questions. The questions for Quant looked good, but please use your judgment and maybe do a trial beforehand.
This was the first result from a simple google search for GMAT classes in Mumbai. But overall the classes didn't help me much. There were many important topics which I think weren't covered in the class. Topics such as idioms for sentence correction were not discussed,  practice on "sentence meaning" in sentence correction, techniques in RC were not taught, and for CR techniques like the negation technique in Assumptions and the yes/no technique for evaluation were taught, but reasoning , cause-effect, and practice on hard questions was not sufficient. Practice was provided for major CR type questions though.Resources given were several homework sheets and to do in class sheets,  verbal question bank ( 200 questions, but more like grammar practice), and online tests. The online verbal practice material was easier compared to the actual GMAT and the GMAT prep software. The exercises for basic grammar were okay, but they are not enough for a hard sentence correction question.

Overall, it gave me a start for my studies, but covering major topics and finding tough questions was something I had to do on my own, I realized that after giving GMAT. I had joined the classes presuming that I can give gmat in 1.5 month after completing a 1 month crash course(20hrs) using this class; however, now I have realized that if the amount I had spent for these classes (~20k Rs), had been spent to do self study using books and online tests ( Powerscore CR bible, Manhattan SC guide, Aristotle SC grail, Manhattan RC guide) with a little more time given to self study, then my GMAT results could have been better. I relied too much on these classes which could also be a mistake. This review could be true for all verbal crash course gmat experiences. Hence, I suggest please use your own judgemnet. Thanks for reading, and best of luck for your exams.

featured_reviews.name: Nimai Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s not just about coaching classes. It’s about people. Moments. The ones that quietly hold you when you’re falling apart.

When I joined IMS, I thought I was just signing up for lectures and practice papers. But what I found was something far more meaningful — mentors who became friends, and strangers who turned into brothers.

Kapil Sir.
I still remember his first lecture. He casually mentioned he graduated from IIT Bombay, and then asked us, “Why did you choose this path? What made you take up Business?” That one question wasn’t just academic, it struck a chord. His presence was magnetic, calm, and healing. Even a minute with him could ease the heaviest mental storms.

I’ve had days where I isolated myself, thinking that would help me study better. But the moment I opened my math book, I’d feel lost again. Not once did Kapil Sir make me feel like a failure. He didn’t just teach, he stayed. With every silly doubt, every anxious thought, and even during the small moments (over farsan snacks or a shared laugh) he was there. More than a mentor, he became the elder brother I never knew I needed.

This post isn’t because he asked me to write one. It’s because I owe him so much more than words

And then there’s Amar Sir.

The mentor who never kept a boundary. Who didn’t treat me like a student, but like a friend. Who reminded me without ever saying it out loud that I wasn’t walking this path alone.

You don’t come across people like this often. Teachers who don’t just clock in hours but invest heart and soul into a student’s dreams. Teachers who aren’t just building careers, but characters. Teachers who choose people over paychecks.

Amar Sir, you’re a man to be crowned. Thank you for standing by me when I didn’t even believe in myself. For celebrating my smallest wins and holding me up during my hardest days.

While IMS might officially provides six-eight MyPlan sessions, I must have had countless hours of guidance and warmth, and through conversations with Kapil Sir and Amar Sir. And those hours were more than sessions. They were lifelines.

To Nishtha Ma’am, Deepak Sir, Manav Sir, Debdeep Sir, Ashish Sir, Ankit Sir and Vinaya Ma’am, you’ve all been more than just names in a system. You’ve been the light that guided me through the darkest corners of this journey. Each of you made me stronger, braver, and better than I was yesterday.

A thank you to the people who held me up when I didn’t think I could go on.
Because sometimes, the right guidance doesn’t just change your score, it changes your story.
